Story ideas

  • Team THRUST (1501) won the Mishawaka and Lafayette district events and reached the World Championship (Archimedes).
  • Olympus Robotics (4982) won the Columbus district event.
  • CyBears (10434) won the Mishawaka district event in only its second season.
  • PhyXTGears (1720) earned a trip to the World Championship (Daly) in Houston.
  • Regional teams won 9 judged awards in 2026, from Innovation in Control to Rising All-Star.
  • In FTC, Canterbury High School's random() (22331) and Madison-Grant Jr./Sr. High School's MG (Microchips & Guac) (25638) return, and R.Amp Robotics (36124) debuts this season.
  • Did Not Field. Yet. 153 schools within 60 miles of downtown Fort Wayne have no school-affiliated FTC or FRC team. The REFINERY wants them on the leaderboard and lists them, with their superintendents and principals, on the main page.

How the sport works

FRC (FIRST Robotics Competition) is for grades 9–12 and uses industrial-size robots; FTC (FIRST Tech Challenge) is for grades 7–12 with smaller robots. Matches pit a red alliance against a blue alliance, three FRC teams per side, and partners change every qualifying match. Top teams pick partners for the playoffs. Indiana FRC teams earn district points at two district events; the leaders advance to the state championship and the FIRST Championship in Houston.

Rankings on this site: the standings follow official FIRST Indiana district points. The power ranking uses Statbotics EPA (Expected Points Added), an estimate of the points a robot adds to its alliance each match. FTC ratings (OPR) are separate and not comparable to EPA.

About The REFINERY

The REFINERY is a nonprofit robotics makerspace in Fort Wayne, Indiana, affiliated with BioNanomics. It helps youth FIRST robotics teams across 12 Northeast Indiana counties with funding, parts, tools, practice space and training, and helps schools start new teams. refineryrobotics.org
